\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{حطام} (ḥuṭām)}{حطام (ḥuṭām)}]{\ar{حطام} (ḥuṭām) — wreckage, debris}

\label{lesson:AR-C354-hutam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to break into, then the Arabic for to spread.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{حطام}}
\textbf{\ar{حطام}} — \emph{ḥuṭām} — \textquotedblleft{}wreckage, debris\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{بحث} \ar{الرجال} \ar{في} \ar{حطام} \ar{السيارة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{baḥatha ar-rijāl fī ḥuṭām as-sayyāra.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The men searched the wreckage of the car.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{حطام}} (\emph{ḥuṭām}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ḥ-ṭ-m} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to break a dry thing in pieces\textquotedblright{}; \emph{ḥuṭām} is what is left in pieces.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥuṭām}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḥuṭām}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{baḥatha ar-rijāl fī ḥuṭām as-sayyāra.} — The men searched the wreckage of the car.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to break into, then the Arabic for to spread, then say \emph{ḥuṭām} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{حطام} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Wreckage, debris\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{رماد} (ramād)}{رماد (ramād)}]{\ar{رماد} (ramād) — ash, ashes}

\label{lesson:AR-C354-ramad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to spread, then the Arabic for wreckage.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{رماد}}
\textbf{\ar{رماد}} — \emph{ramād} — \textquotedblleft{}ash, ashes\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{بقي} \ar{الرماد} \ar{في} \ar{المدفأة} \ar{حتى} \ar{الصباح}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{baqiya ar-ramād fī al-midfaʾa ḥattā aṣ-ṣabāḥ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The ash stayed in the stove until morning.
\end{quote}

The taught \ar{رمادي}, grey, is the colour of ash.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{رماد}} (\emph{ramād}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-m-d} (Lane), where \emph{ramād} is ashes; the taught \emph{ramādī}, grey, is \textquotedblleft{}ash-coloured\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ramād}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ramād}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{baqiya ar-ramād fī al-midfaʾa ḥattā aṣ-ṣabāḥ.} — The ash stayed in the stove until morning.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to spread, then the Arabic for wreckage, then say \emph{ramād} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{رماد} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Ash, ashes\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{شرارة} (sharāra)}{شرارة (sharāra)}]{\ar{شرارة} (sharāra) — a spark}

\label{lesson:AR-C354-sharara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for wreckage, then the Arabic for ash.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{شرارة}}
\textbf{\ar{شرارة}} — \emph{sharāra} — \textquotedblleft{}a spark\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{بدأ} \ar{الحريق} \ar{من} \ar{شرارة} \ar{صغيرة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{badaʾa al-ḥarīq min sharāra ṣaghīra.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The fire started from a small spark.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{شرارة}} (\emph{sharāra}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{sh-r-r} (Lane), where Lane gives \emph{sharar} as sparks flying from a fire, beside \emph{sharr}, evil.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sharāra}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sharāra}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{badaʾa al-ḥarīq min sharāra ṣaghīra.} — The fire started from a small spark.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for wreckage, then the Arabic for ash, then say \emph{sharāra} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{شرارة} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A spark\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{لهب} (lahab)}{لهب (lahab)}]{\ar{لهب} (lahab) — a flame, flames}

\label{lesson:AR-C354-lahab}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for ash, then the Arabic for a spark.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{لهب}}
\textbf{\ar{لهب}} — \emph{lahab} — \textquotedblleft{}a flame, flames\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{رأينا} \ar{لهب} \ar{النار} \ar{من} \ar{بعيد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{raʾaynā lahab an-nār min baʿīd.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We saw the flames of the fire from far away.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{لهب}} (\emph{lahab}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{l-h-b} (Lane), \textquotedblleft{}to blaze up\textquotedblright{}; \emph{lahab} is the tongue of the fire.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{تسرب} (tasarraba)}{تسرب (tasarraba)}]{\ar{تسرب} (tasarraba) — to leak, to seep}

\label{lesson:AR-C354-tasarraba}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a spark, then the Arabic for a flame.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{تسرب}}
\textbf{\ar{تسرب}} — \emph{tasarraba} — \textquotedblleft{}to leak, to seep\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تسرب} \ar{الماء} \ar{من} \ar{السقف}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tasarraba al-māʾ min as-saqf.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Water leaked through the ceiling.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يتسرب}, \emph{yatasarrab}.

Of news: \ar{تسرب} \ar{الخبر}, the news leaked out.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{تسرب}} (\emph{tasarraba}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{s-r-b} (Lane), where \emph{sarab} is a burrow or tunnel under the ground. It is Form V, \textquotedblleft{}to pass in, little by little\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tasarraba}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tasarraba}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tasarraba al-māʾ min as-saqf.} — Water leaked through the ceiling.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a spark, then the Arabic for a flame, then say \emph{tasarraba} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{تسرب} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To leak, to seep\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
